nodes.name: Next-attempt webhook
nodes.notes: Meant to be called by call-wrap-up.workflow.json right after a rep submits their required disposition (new this pass) - the rep's manually-entered Disposition is now the authoritative input here, not an AI guess (post-call-synthesis's own Disposition output is now QA-only, see W3.4's notes). Input contract: {hopperEntryId, opportunityId, disposition, attemptCountThisWave, wave (1-2, was 1-4), lastAttemptDate, firstAttemptDateThisWave, attemptCountToday, repId, scheduledAt}. firstAttemptDateThisWave/attemptCountToday/scheduledAt are new this pass - see 'Apply attempt matrix's own notes for the cadence rewrite that needs them.

nodes.name: Apply attempt matrix
nodes.notes: The one workflow in this library with real, business-specified cadence logic encoded directly (not a placeholder) - rewritten this pass per Jonathan's explicit two-wave/day-cap instruction, replacing the earlier 6/4/8-attempt, 4-wave, 90-120-day model. Every branch decides the HopperEntry's next state (hopperStatus/claimedByRepId/nextOwner/attemptCountToday/etc.) alongside the human-readable action, since 'Write HopperEntry state' (below) needs a decision to persist, not just a decision to report back to the caller.

nodes.name: Write HopperEntry state

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: $json.hopperStatus, claimedByRepId: $json.claimedByRepId, disposition: $('Next-attempt webhook').item.json.body.disposition, attemptCountThisWave: $json.attemptCountThisWave !== undefined ? $json.attemptCountThisWave : $('Next-attempt webhook').item.json.body.attemptCountThisWave, wave: $json.nextWave || $('Next-attempt webhook').item.json.body.wave, lastAttemptDate: new Date().toISOString(), firstAttemptDateThisWave: $json.firstAttemptDateThisWave !== undefined ? $json.firstAttemptDateThisWave : $('Next-attempt webhook').item.json.body.firstAttemptDateThisWave, attemptCountToday: $json.attemptCountToday, nextEligibleAt: $json.nextEligibleAt || null }) }}

nodes.notes: NEW this pass - previously this workflow only computed a decision and responded with it, it never persisted anything, because HopperEntry didn't exist as an object until this pass (CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md). Skipped entirely for the REVIEW action's hopperStatus: null case below via the IF node, since there's nothing decided yet to write - a human needs to look at it first, and the entry stays exactly as claimed/Claimed in the meantime rather than being touched.

nodes.name: Needs a write?
nodes.notes: REVIEW (unrecognized disposition) sets hopperStatus: null on purpose - nothing safe to write yet, needs a human look first. Everything else always has a real hopperStatus to persist.
